final_answer: The proposal is unreliable. Behind a same-host reverse proxy the client IP is the proxy (127.0.0.1), and many agents share egress IPs, so identity cannot be inferred. X-Forwarded-For is spoofable unless only the trusted proxy sets it. Design: give each agent its own credential (token or mTLS certificate with an agent_id claim), verified at the proxy, which sets a signed identity header. The endpoint accepts identity only from the proxy and logs it with request IDs.
plan_steps: Reject IP-based identity and document the reason
Issue a unique credential per agent with scoped permissions
Configure the proxy to verify credentials and strip any client-supplied identity headers
Configure the endpoint to trust forwarded identity only from the proxy socket or loopback address
Log verified agent identity alongside request IDs in both proxy and application logs
actions_requiring_human_approval: Issuing or rotating credentials for agents
Changing proxy trust settings in production
